lesson.text: Verbal irony is saying the opposite of what you mean: stepping into a puddle and saying "Great, just what I needed."
Situational irony is when the opposite of what you expect happens: a fire station burns down.
A pun plays on a word with two meanings or two words that sound alike: "The bicycle couldn't stand up by itself because it was two-tyred."
Writers use irony and puns for humour, criticism or surprise.
